title: DbDataBuild project configuration
description: dbdatabuild.yml at the project root. Offline settings only: credentials are never stored here, they come from the runtime environment. Every key is optional; an absent key takes the built-in default, which every command prints in its header. This schema is for editors; `dbdatabuild validate` applies the same rules with diagnostic codes.

defaults.description: Model settings every model inherits from this file; a folder's _dbdatabuild.yml has the same section and layers onto it, and a model's own file layers on top (the nearest wins). A list appends, a mapping merges by key, a scalar replaces; a key suffix changes that for the key: `key=` replaces what was inherited, `key-` removes the listed items or keys, `key+` merges (the default). The settings themselves are those of a model file (model.schema.json); they are checked where they are merged into a model.

connections.description: Connections a model is built on when its own file and the folders above it say nothing different. Default: [sqlserver]. Lists append: a model that lists its own connections adds to these unless it writes `connections=`.

Named database endpoints. A connection named after an engine (sqlserver, fabric, postgres) exists without being declared; declaring it sets its version. Any other name needs an `engine`. The name is part of the login's environment variable: DBDATABUILD_<NAME>_READ and _WRITE.

sqlserver.description: The connection named after the engine `sqlserver`: it needs no declaration, and an entry only sets its version.

version.description: The engine's major version, or the T-SQL level to generate for: 16 for SQL Server 2022 (and a 2025 server at compatibility level 160), 17 for 2025 at level 170. Lets the matrix linter resolve min_version rows.

parameters.description: Values this connection carries, which differ between connections of one application (a store id, a region). Referenced as `${connection.name}`, or `${origin.name}` by a copy that reads from the connection. Names are lowercase words with underscores; values are single values, read as text.

tracking_schema.description: Schema for the tracking tables. Default: dbdatabuild.

string_semantics.description: The project's string comparison profile (DESIGN.md 7.4). Default: case-insensitive, accent-sensitive, trailing spaces ignored (SQL Server style).

collations.description: Logical collation name to per-engine collation name.

severity.description: Severity of matrix findings. `unsupported` findings are always errors and cannot be configured.

hook_groups.description: Named, ordered sets of hooks that models reference with `use: <group>`. Groups do not nest. Hook names inside a group are prefixed with the group name in plans (`group.name`).

metadata.description: Metadata stored in the target for introspection (`publish-metadata`). `store_on_apply: true` also stores the project and the applied models' documents, and the plan, after every successful `apply`. Default false.

lowering.description: Model queries are bound by DuckDB and lowered to one explicit query before they are checked and transpiled (committed under rendered/lowered/). `enabled: false` turns that stage off and transpiles the author's SQL directly, as before; there is no per-model fallback. Default true.

lint.description: Advisory lints. `indexes: false` turns off the index advice (DDB-223, DDB-224) and `slices: false` the slice advice (DDB-225) for the whole project; a model can silence single codes with `lint_ignore`. Both default to true.

rewrites.description: Which rewrites make the engines give DuckDB's answers (`dbdatabuild matrix --rewrites` lists them). The default is `fidelity: exact`: all of them. `fidelity: native` turns off every rewrite the targets can do without, for shorter queries and simpler plans, at the price of each engine's own behavior (a trailing space not counted, an integer cut instead of rounded, a week counted another way); `disable` and `enable` change single rewrites. A rewrite a target cannot do without (SQL Server has no LPAD, PostgreSQL's round takes no double) cannot be turned off (DDB-229). A model's section is applied on top of the project's.

hook.title: hook
hook.description: A native-SQL script attached to a plan event. `script` is one path, or a path per target; the file is executed exactly as committed. The list order is the run order.

event.description: pre_ or post_ create, alter, load or backfill. pre_drop and post_drop are reserved: the planner has no drop step yet, so they are refused.

effect.description: What the script may do: ddl (default) or data. `run` runs only data hooks.

risk.description: The author's declaration, which sets the plan step's risk class. Default safe.

connectionOfAnEngine.description: Any other connection: it names its engine.

version.description: The engine's major version, or the T-SQL level to generate for: 16 for SQL Server 2022 (and a 2025 server at compatibility level 160), 17 for 2025 at level 170. Lets the matrix linter resolve min_version rows.
